---
title: "From LLMs to Agents"
subtitle: "What the model is, how it is built, and how it begins to act"
---

This site supports a 35–40 minute conceptual talk and a standalone
learning resource for readers who are comfortable following mathematical
ideas but may not use them every day, prepared as background for a
later, more applied Claude Code workshop. It is co-produced with Claude
Code under human review: Claude Code drafts and runs deterministic
checks; a human reviewer approves substantive choices, final wording, and
every commit.

::: {.callout-important}
## This site is still under construction

This site currently contains **three** complete learning modules and
**three** of the eventual talk's slides — enough to prove that the
website, the deck, and the browser-based interactive all work together,
offline, from one set of sources. It is not the finished course. The
remaining modules, the full talk, and the curated resource library are
planned but not yet built.
:::

## How the two products relate

**The website is the primary, standalone learning product.** Someone who
never attends the talk should be able to learn the material from the site
alone, with the full mathematics, worked examples, and an interactive
laboratory. The live talk is a carefully selected, lower-math path through
this material: about 35–40 minutes, naming and defining every required
term, but carrying no required live equation and no required live
demonstration — both live in full on the site, which the talk points to
rather than reproduces.

## Available now

- [**The short story**](short-story.qmd) — the whole course in about ten
  minutes: one mental model from the text you type to a system that uses
  tools, with a link into the lesson that develops each step. Start here.
- [**From text to numbers**](learn/how-created.qmd) — what has to happen
  before a language model can learn from text: tokens, token IDs,
  embedding vectors, and next-token targets, traced through one sentence.
- [**Neurons, layers, and learning**](learn/neural-networks.qmd) — a
  complete, standalone module on parameterized functions, gradient descent,
  and backpropagation, with a fully worked and independently
  numerically-checked example.
- [**Why transformers**](learn/why-transformers.qmd) — a complete,
  standalone module on the sequence-processing problem self-attention was
  built to solve, with a worked example checked against the original
  paper's own stated bounds.
- [**Deep dive: how self-attention moves information**](learn/transformers-attention.qmd)
  — optional; queries, keys, values, causal masking, multi-head
  attention, and where attention sits inside a transformer block, with a
  worked numerical example.
- [**Softmax, sampling, and temperature**](learn/softmax-sampling.qmd) — a
  complete, standalone learning module, including a live softmax-and-
  sampling laboratory and a no-JavaScript fallback.
- [**How pretraining works**](learn/training.qmd) — the autoregressive
  objective, negative log-likelihood, the optimization loop, what
  pretraining does and does not teach, and how it differs from
  post-training and from inference-time context.
- [**Post-training**](learn/posttraining.qmd) — how a pretrained model
  becomes an assistant: supervised instruction tuning, preference-based
  methods (reward-model and direct routes), model-generated feedback,
  reasoning-oriented reinforcement learning, and why none of it is a
  system prompt.
- [**From assistant to agent**](learn/agents.qmd) — what a tool call
  actually is, the workflow-versus-agent distinction, the agent loop,
  state and memory, reusable procedures, verification, and permissions,
  with a coding agent as the running example.
- [**Using models well**](learn/using-models-well.qmd) — the practical
  guide: task selection, task specification, context, source of truth,
  tools, verification, bounded units, handoffs, model selection, and an
  operating checklist, each tied to a mechanism taught earlier.
- [**Deep dive: tokens, embeddings, and the context window**](learn/tokens-context.qmd)
  — optional; why models use subword units, what the embedding table does
  and does not encode, and what a finite context window implies in
  practice.
- [**Slides**](slides/llms-to-agents.qmd) — three slides from an earlier
  prototype iteration of the talk design (logits and softmax, training and
  maximum likelihood, sampling and temperature). Left as a historical
  checkpoint; not rebuilt to the current talk design in this batch.
- [**Resources**](resources.qmd) — the sources used so far, annotated.

## Sources

Every substantive factual claim on this site carries a claim ID that
resolves in `sources/claims.csv`, described in prose in
`sources/source-map.md`. Both files are checked automatically against the
rendered pages.
